sentences.text: This small dinosaur measured about 1.5 meters in length and weighed approximately 22.5 kilograms.
It possessed a long, slender neck and tail, features similar to other early sauropodomorphs.
Histological analysis of the humerus and femur suggests the holotype was a fast-growing individual, possibly less than one year old.
Ignavusaurus fossils were found in the Upper Elliot Formation, dating to approximately 200 million years ago during the Early Jurassic.
The holotype specimen was discovered in southern Lesotho near the locality known as Ha Ralekoala.
The genus was described based on a partial but well-preserved articulated skeleton.
The fossils were found mostly articulated, but the skull was badly damaged and broken into more than 120 fragments.
The type species Ignavusaurus rachelis was formally described in 2010 by the Spanish paleontologist F. Knoll.
The remains were mentioned in an unpublished 2002 doctoral dissertation but remained formally undescribed for several years.
The fossils were temporarily catalogued as BM HR 20 at the National Museum of Natural History in Paris.
Ignavusaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph, a type of long-necked, herbivorous saurischian dinosaur.
It is placed within the family Massospondylidae.
Ignavusaurus lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
Some researchers suggest that Ignavusaurus might be synonymous with Massospondylus, arguing that its primitive features are actually juvenile traits.
Other cladistic analyses have found Ignavusaurus to be a valid genus most closely related to Sarahsaurus within the group Massopoda.
